subject.title: [improvement] Sub-agent cascade circuit breaker for multi-agent team reliability

question: What subagent breaker contract should OpenClaw core own: a persisted per-agent/task circuit breaker in `sessions_spawn`, a narrower extension of existing session/tool guards, or deferral to existing plugin/hooks until a broader health model is designed?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent behavior crosses new config, persisted runtime state, failure taxonomy, operator UX, and overlap with existing retry/failover/loop protections, so automation should not choose the product contract.

options.title: Design a core subagent health breaker
options.body: Define persisted failure receipt scope, classification, cooldown or half-open semantics, parent-visible error shape, override/reset behavior, and CLI/UI surfacing before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader session-health work
options.body: Treat this as a subagent-specific slice of the open session-level breaker design and avoid a separate subagent-only policy surface.

options.title: Keep as plugin/hook guidance for now
options.body: Document current hook/plugin workaround patterns and defer core changes until maintainers want a first-class breaker API.

recommendation.title: Design a core subagent health breaker
recommendation.body: Define persisted failure receipt scope, classification, cooldown or half-open semantics, parent-visible error shape, override/reset behavior, and CLI/UI surfacing before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history shows repeated adjacent work on subagent control, registry helpers, and product-sensitive runtime boundaries, making this the best routing candidate for the contract choice.
